items.abstract: <jats:p>Physics-informed neural networks struggle with inadequate localized resolution when solutions exhibit steep gradients, sharp peaks, or fine-scale oscillations. Static collocation points cannot adapt to spatially varying solution features. We propose residual equidistribution driven adaptive sampling (REDAS), which dynamically redistributes sampling points to achieve an equidistribution of residuals within the computational domain. By identifying collocation points in low residual regions and moving them to high residual regions, REDAS gradually balancing the residual distribution over the domain. This not only reduces the overall approximation error but also avoids the occurrence of under sampled regions. Numerical experiments on Poisson, Helmholtz, and Allen-Cahn equations demonstrate consistent accuracy improvements over static sampling, with relative $L^2$ error reductions up to one order of magnitude . The method also exhibits reduced sensitivity to hyperparameters and more consistent performance across repeated runs.</jats:p>
title: Residual Equidistribution Driven Adaptive Sampling algorithm for Physics Informed Neural Networks

items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper establishes an approximation theorem for randomized neural networks (RaNNs) whose hidden-layer parameters are uniformly sampled from a prescribed bounded domain. Our analysis shows that, for RaNNs of the form $\mathop{\sum}_i W_i \sigma(A_i, b_i)$, the size of the sampling domain required to achieve optimal approximation is intrinsically linked to the smoothness of the target function and the number of neurons. Motivated by this theoretical insight, we integrate a partition of unity (PoU) with RaNNs to develop an adaptive physics-informed randomized neural network (PIRaNN) method for solving partial differential equations with limited local regularity. The proposed adaptive strategy refines the PoU based on a posteriori error indicators, enabling the network to efficiently capture localized solution features. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical results and demonstrate the strong approximation capabilities of RaNNs, confirming the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed adaptive PIRaNN method.</jats:p>
title: Adaptive Randomized Neural Networks with Locally Activation Function: Theory and Algorithm for Solving PDEs
